name: CA-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 21 points, one of the bluest House seats
Incumbent Laura Friedman holds a massive cash advantage ($469k vs $2.6k)
Challenger Scott Meyers raised under $60k with no outside spending
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+21 district, a sitting incumbent, and a roughly 14-to-1 fundraising edge leave the Republican challenger without a plausible path. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability, the expected margin stays near 25 points.
model.watch: A sharply lower-turnout electorate or an unexpected late influx of outside money for Meyers could narrow the margin, though an outright flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 30th District sits in the San Fernando Valley and leans Democratic by about 21 points, among the bluer House seats in the country. First-term incumbent Laura Friedman advanced to the general election and faces Republican Scott Meyers, a little-known challenger. Friedman has raised roughly $828,000 and holds about $469,000 on hand, while Meyers has raised under $60,000 with about $2,600 remaining and no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent. The fundamentals — the district's heavy Democratic lean, incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage — all point in the same direction. The expected margin is roughly 25 points, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than the outcome itself.
